parts.passageSubtitle: The people below are all looking for a weekend workshop or class. Read the descriptions of eight workshops (A–H).

passage.text: The people below all want to join a weekend workshop. Decide which workshop would be the most suitable for each person.

passage.label: A
passage.text: Clay Studio — This friendly class is ideal for complete beginners who want to try making pottery on a wheel. A teacher shows you each step, from shaping a simple bowl to adding glaze. Materials are included, and finished pieces can be collected the following week.

passage.label: B
passage.text: Mountain Lens — Spend a weekend walking in the hills with a professional photographer. You will practise using your own camera to take clear landscape pictures in natural light. The group stops often, so there is plenty of time for advice and trying different views.

passage.label: C
passage.text: The Rustic Oven — Learn how to prepare sourdough bread and bake it in a traditional outdoor stone oven. This workshop welcomes beginners and includes all ingredients. At lunchtime, everyone sits together to enjoy soup, salad, and warm bread made during the morning session.

passage.label: D
passage.text: Wood & Craft — This practical carpentry course teaches beginners how to measure, cut, and join wood safely. You will build a small stool or chair to take home. The workshop provides safety equipment, wood, and professional hand tools, so you do not need to bring anything.

passage.label: E
passage.text: Urban Sprout — Discover how to grow organic vegetables and useful herbs in small spaces such as balconies and patios. The tutor explains composting, seed planting, and choosing containers. You will leave with a tray of young plants and a simple plan for your own home garden.

passage.label: F
passage.text: Silver Spoon — This advanced baking class is designed for confident home cooks who already know the basics. A professional pastry chef demonstrates cake decoration, delicate fillings, and presentation techniques. Participants should bring an apron and expect to work quickly throughout the afternoon.

passage.label: G
passage.text: Green Earth Farm — Spend a day on a working organic farm and learn about large fields, crop rotation, and machinery. Visitors help with simple outdoor jobs and watch experienced farmers using tractors. This course is best for people interested in farming as a career.

passage.label: H
passage.text: Canvas & Color — Join an open-air painting class beside the river. The tutor focuses on portraits and oil colours, helping creative hobbyists improve their technique. Some experience is useful, but all paints, brushes, and boards are provided for the day.

questionGroups.instruction: For each question, choose the correct answer.

questions.prompt: Daniel wants to learn how to bake artisan bread in a traditional outdoor oven. He would prefer a weekend workshop where beginners are welcome, lunch is included, and he can taste the food he has helped to make.

Hannah is looking for an introductory pottery class where she can make something useful with her hands. She has never tried this activity before, so she needs a patient teacher, all the materials provided, and a finished piece to collect later.

Leo wants to improve his photography while spending time outdoors. He already owns a camera and would like a professional to show him how to take better pictures of hills, paths, and wide natural views during a weekend activity.

Maya has a small balcony at home and wants to grow vegetables and herbs without using chemicals. She is not interested in large farm machines, but she would like practical advice about containers, compost, and starting plants from seed.

Oliver is interested in learning a traditional craft and wants to make a piece of furniture he can keep. He needs a course for beginners where safety equipment, wood, and proper tools are all supplied by the organiser.

parts.passageTitle: Part 3 — My Life as a Weather Forecaster
parts.passageSubtitle: Read the text and questions below. For each question, choose the correct answer.

passage.text: A weather forecaster explains how a childhood interest became her career.

People often ask me why I chose a career in meteorology. Growing up in a windy coastal town, I spent hours watching massive storm clouds roll across the ocean. While other kids ran indoors when it started to pour, I stayed outside, fascinated by the sudden change in atmosphere. That childhood curiosity eventually led me to study physics and environmental science at university, turning my lifelong hobby into a professional job.

Working at the national weather center is never boring, but it requires keeping unusual hours. My alarm usually rings at 3:00 AM because I need to prepare the early morning broadcast before commuters head to work. When I arrive at the office, I analyze satellite maps, computer simulations, and wind speed data. Predicting the weather is like solving a complex puzzle where the pieces are constantly shifting.

The most stressful part of the job is forecasting unexpected weather events, such as sudden heavy snowstorms or summer heatwaves. A few years ago, computer models indicated that a mild weekend was approaching. However, by monitoring radar updates closely, I noticed a sudden change in pressure and warned local authorities about an incoming gale just hours before it struck. That accurate prediction prevented numerous accidents on coastal roads.

Despite the early mornings and high-pressure moments, I find immense satisfaction in helping people stay safe and prepared. There is nothing quite like looking out the window and seeing that your forecast has helped someone choose the right jacket or plan a safe journey. Meteorology has taught me to appreciate the incredible power of nature every single day.

passage.text:
My Life in a Tiny House

Three years ago, I decided to leave my large, expensive suburban house and move into a self-built tiny home on wheels. For most of my adult life, I had accumulated boxes of unnecessary items that I rarely used. (16) ........ I wanted a simpler lifestyle that allowed me to spend my money on experiences rather than rent and utility bills.

Designing the layout was the most difficult part of the project. Every single centimeter counted, so furniture had to serve multiple purposes. My sofa folded out into a bed, and the staircase contained hidden storage drawers for my clothes. (17) ........ Building it took six months of hard work during my weekends and holidays.

Once the house was finished, parking it legally proved to be another challenge. (18) ........ Eventually, I found a friendly local farmer who agreed to rent me a small corner of his land overlooking a peaceful valley.

Living in a small space has completely changed my daily habits. Because I have very little room, I cannot buy things on impulse anymore. (19) ........ I also spend much more time outdoors walking in nature instead of watching television indoors.

Moving into a tiny house was certainly a bold step, but I have never regretted it. (20) ........ It taught me that happiness does not come from owning a large property, but from living with purpose and freedom.

passage.text:
The Honeybee's Secret Language

For centuries, scientists have been amazed by the complex behavior of honeybees. When a worker bee discovers a rich source of nectar flowers, it returns to the hive to share the news. It performs a special circular movement known (21) ........ the waggle dance to communicate the exact location to other bees.

The dance tells the colony both the direction and the distance of the food flowers relative to the sun. Other bees watch the movements closely inside the dark hive before flying straight (22) ........ the target. This remarkable communication system ensures that the colony can gather food efficiently.

However, honeybee populations face serious threats today due to habitat loss and pesticide use. Many environmental organizations are working hard to protect bees and encourage gardeners to plant flowers that provide vital (23) ........ for pollinators. Without bees, many fruits and vegetables we eat every day would simply (24) ........ to grow. Protecting these tiny insects is essential to maintaining a healthy ecosystem and ensuring a sustainable (25) ........ for our global food supply (26) .........

Learning a New Language

Many adults dream (27) ........ speaking a second language fluently, but they often believe it is too difficult to start later in life. However, modern research shows that learning a foreign language at any age brings wonderful cognitive benefits.

The secret to success is consistency rather (28) ........ studying for hours once a week. Practising a little bit (29) ........ single day helps your brain retain vocabulary much faster. Listening to podcasts, watching foreign films, or chatting with native speakers online are great ways to immerse yourself in the culture.

Remember that making mistakes is a natural part (30) ........ the learning process. If you are afraid (31) ........ making errors, you will never speak fluently. Be patient with (32) ........ and enjoy the rewarding journey of communication.
